Concrete Driveways · Maitland, FL

Pouring a Concrete Driveway in Maitland

A concrete driveway in Maitland runs $6–$15 per sq ft installed, the market range as of this October. The city's own $175 driveway/sidewalk permit applies before the first form goes up, and a job over $5,000 needs a recorded Notice of Commencement ahead of the first inspection.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

A $175 city permit, plus the paperwork that comes with it

Maitland's fee schedule lists a driveway or sidewalk permit at $175, filed through Community Development rather than Orange County's building division (City of Maitland, Building and Permitting Fees). The application packet calls for the signed permit checklist, a Limited Power of Attorney form, an Owner/Builder Affidavit if applicable, and a Waiver of Limitations Affidavit, and any job over $5,000 needs a Notice of Commencement recorded before the first inspection (City of Maitland, Permitting Information).

Seventy percent of the lot, driveway and all

Maitland's RSF-1, RSF-2 and RSF-3 single-family districts share the same 70 percent impervious-coverage ceiling, with the driveway counted alongside the house, pool and any patio toward that one number (City of Maitland LDC, Art. 3 Zone Districts). That's a noticeably higher cap than Winter Park's 50 percent next door, which gives a wider driveway more room on a comparably sized Maitland lot before the math gets tight.

Grading the Driveway Away From the Garage Slab

A driveway that slopes toward the garage instead of away from it sends every afternoon storm straight at the house. Florida code requires fill to be compacted for uniform support, and part of getting that right is shaping the subgrade so water sheets off the surface and away from the foundation rather than pooling at the threshold. On a flat Maitland lot, that sometimes means building the far edge of the driveway up slightly more than the garage end, even when the difference is not visible to the eye. It matters most on flatwoods soils that already hold water close to the surface for months at a time.

What a Permit Inspection Actually Checks Before the Pour

Where Maitland or the county requires a permit for the work, an inspector typically looks at the job before concrete gets poured, not after, checking things like form layout, base material and any reinforcement going in. That review happens at the forming stage, which is one more reason forming and base work take real time rather than getting rushed. A failed or delayed inspection pushes the pour date back, so we schedule the inspection early in the process to protect the rest of the timeline. Jurisdictions differ in exactly what gets checked, so confirming the local process before we mobilize avoids a surprise delay.

Widening a driveway on a 1990s-era Maitland lot, worked out in square feet

Say a Maitland home built close to the city's 1996 median construction year widens its original 10 by 20 foot driveway, 200 square feet, to a 20 by 24 foot two-car layout, 480 square feet. At $6–$15 per sq ft installed, that upgrade runs roughly $2,880 to $7,200 before the $175 permit fee, and because the contract value clears $5,000, a Notice of Commencement has to be recorded before the city's first inspection of the job.

Why a 4-Inch Slab Isn't Enough for a Boat Trailer

A standard 4-inch driveway is built for cars and light trucks, not for an RV, a boat trailer or anything that concentrates weight on a narrow set of wheels. For that kind of load, we take the slab to 5 or 6 inches thick, which spreads the weight over more concrete and resists the point-load cracking a thinner slab would show first. Anyone in Maitland planning to park something heavier than a daily driver should say so before the forms go in, since thickening a finished driveway later means tearing it out. Mix strength matters too, but added thickness does more for a point load than extra psi alone.

Irrigation Heads Aimed at the Driveway Cause Slow Damage

A sprinkler head that has drifted even slightly over the years can end up soaking the edge of a driveway every time the zone runs, and that repeated wetting works against a compacted base the same way standing rainwater would, just more predictably. It also leaves mineral staining on the concrete surface that gets worse with every cycle. On a Maitland lot, it is worth checking irrigation head aim against the new driveway's footprint before the first watering cycle after the pour, since a head that was fine aimed at an old garden bed is not necessarily fine aimed at fresh concrete and a compacted edge that has not fully settled yet.

Reading Rainy Season Numbers Before the Storms Start

Orlando averages about 51.45 inches of rain a year and Sarasota-Bradenton about 49.05, most of it concentrated in a rainy season that typically runs from late May into October. Before that season starts, it is worth walking a Maitland driveway and clearing leaves, mulch and sand out of the control joints, since a joint packed with debris cannot channel water the way an open one does. Standing water that collects against a slab edge because a joint is clogged works on the base underneath over an entire wet season, not just one storm, which is a slower version of the same settlement problem poor compaction causes.

Frequently asked questions

What does a Maitland driveway permit cost?

The city's fee schedule lists a driveway/sidewalk permit at $175, filed with the Community Development Department rather than Orange County's office.

When does a Maitland driveway job need a Notice of Commencement?

Any job valued over $5,000 needs a recorded Notice of Commencement before the city's first inspection, a threshold Maitland adopted effective October 1, 2023.

How much wider can a Maitland driveway be before hitting the coverage cap?

All three single-family zoning districts allow up to 70 percent total impervious coverage, counting the driveway along with the house, pool and patio, a higher ceiling than several neighboring Orange County cities.
